previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of spinal cord injury, paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, and chronic indwelling Foley catheter was admitted for worsening left flank and hypogastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and chills, two days after incomplete treatment of a prior urinary tract infection. She had stopped her previous course of nitrofurantoin after seven days. In the hospital, she was started on IV antibiotics, received IV hydration, and had her Foley catheter changed. Urine culture grew Enterococcus sensitive to nitrofurantoin, and renal ultrasound was normal. She improved clinically, remained afebrile, and tolerated oral intake. Her antibiotics were switched to oral nitrofurantoin for a full 11-day course at discharge. She was counseled on alcohol and cocaine use, which were detected in screening, and declined treatment programs. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete her antibiotics, avoid substances, and follow up with her primary care provider.

This is a ___ yo female with a history neurogenic bladder and 
recurrent UTI/pyelo admitted today with symptoms similar to 
previous pyelonephritis.  She also presents with abdominal pain 
and nausea, similar to her previous episodes.

* Abdominal pain/Flank pain - Given her presentation, most 
likley related to recurrent pyelonephritis.  In the ED, she was

continued until the UCx came back positive for E coli, resistent

renal US was negative for hydronephrosis, stone, perinephric

appropriately discharged.  She did not return in order to 
receive antibiotics to complete her course.  Security was called
